text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. Can you describe the nature of the feeding difficulties and when they first started? Also, has the baby had any episodes of vomiting or diarrhea?

speaker: Patient
text: The baby has been very fussy, feeding less than usual, and the abdomen looks distended. Crying gets worse when the belly is touched.

speaker: Doctor
text: Does the baby pass stool, and if so, what is the color and consistency? Have you noticed any blood or mucus in the diaper, or has the baby had any episodes of bilious (green) vomiting?

speaker: Patient
text: There has not been fever, vomiting, or diarrhea like a stomach infection. The baby was born at 39 weeks without birth complications.

speaker: Doctor
text: Is the baby passing any stool, and if so, what is the color and consistency? Have you noticed any blood or mucus in the diaper?

text: The baby did not seem to pass stool normally and the belly swelling has become more obvious. Feeding has clearly decreased over the past few days.

speaker: Doctor
text: I need to confirm if the baby has passed any meconium in the first 48 hours of life, as delayed passage can indicate an underlying obstruction. Additionally, have you noticed any pale, clay-colored stools or a failure to thrive since birth?

speaker: Patient
text: The abdomen still looks swollen and the baby seems uncomfortable, especially in the lower abdomen.
